packet.headline_seed: Call for 'full review' as pressure grows on Infantino
packet.description_seed: The leadership of Fifa is publicly questioned by football's governing bodies in Europe, North and Central America and the Caribbean.

what: Call for 'full review' as pressure grows on Infantino

clean_source_blocks.text: Infantino has been the president of Fifa since February 2016 Gianni Infantino's leadership of Fifa has been publicly questioned by football's governing bodies in Europe, North and Central America and the Caribbean. Uefa and Concacaf both released statements on Saturday criticising the leadership at the world governing body after Infantino said Fifa would no longer proceed with the proposal to sell stakes in their competitions to private investors. Uefa, which governs European football, welcomed the decision to withdraw the plan, describing it as a "victory for the whole game". The body accused of Infantino of failing to deliver on promises, quoting a speech he gave when campaigning to become Fifa president in 2016.
The leadership of Fifa is publicly questioned by football's governing bodies in Europe, North and Central America and the Caribbean.

Concacaf, which oversees football in North, Central America and the Caribbean, followed Uefa in criticising the plans, saying "unity had prevailed" and that the proposals were a "symptom of leadership that has stopped putting football first". "This recent unilateral and egregious act of poor governance and leadership follows a pattern of missteps and similar behaviour. A full review of this leadership must now take place," a Concacaf statement read. Unlike Uefa, Concacaf did not mention Infantino by name. The fallout from the plans means Infantino is now under immense pressure as he seeks re-election for a fourth term as president at the Fifa Congress in March. Uefa were the first major governing body to react to Infantino's decision to drop the investment plans, saying the Swiss had failed to deliver on his promises.

FIFA have abandoned plans to sell a minority stake in its commercial business after serious opposition from the global football community and the withdrawal of key investors (New York Post). It is a major blow to FIFA president Gianni Infantino's leadership. The governing body had been exploring the sale of a one-fifth stake in a newly created commercial entity. The deal would have valued the business at around $20 billion and raised approximately $4.2bn. The proposal involved spinning off FIFA's lucrative television rights, sponsorship agreements, licensing and ticketing operations into a separate company. However, the project has now been abandoned after Thrive Capital, the investment firm led by Joshua Kushner, reportedly pulled back from the negotiations. JP Morgan had been advising on the transaction. They have also closed their involvement as support for the proposal evaporated.

Infantino has been the president of Fifa since February 2016

Gianni Infantino's leadership of Fifa has been publicly questioned by football's governing bodies in Europe, North and Central America and the Caribbean.

Uefa and Concacaf both released statements on Saturday criticising the leadership at the world governing body after Infantino said Fifa would no longer proceed with the proposal to sell stakes in their competitions to private investors.

Uefa, which governs European football, welcomed the decision to withdraw the plan, describing it as a "victory for the whole game".

The body accused of Infantino of failing to deliver on promises, quoting a speech he gave when campaigning to become Fifa president in 2016.

Concacaf, which oversees football in North, Central America and the Caribbean, followed Uefa in criticising the plans, saying "unity had prevailed" and that the proposals were a "symptom of leadership that has stopped putting football first".

"This recent unilateral and egregious act of poor governance and leadership follows a pattern of missteps and similar behaviour. A full review of this leadership must now take place," a Concacaf statement read.

Unlike Uefa, Concacaf did not mention Infantino by name.

The fallout from the plans means Infantino is now under immense pressure as he seeks re-election for a fourth term as president at the Fifa Congress in March.

Uefa were the first major governing body to react to Infantino's decision to drop the investment plans, saying the Swiss had failed to deliver on his promises.

"The current Fifa leadership has not only lost Uefa's confidence but also that of many other members of the football family," Uefa's statement read.

"When Gianni Infantino asked for the trust and the votes of Fifa's member associations to elect him as their president in 2016, he said, 'Of course we have to be transparent'.

"He told the assembled stakeholders, 'The money of Fifa is your money. It's not the money of the Fifa president. You are the national associations and the money of Fifa has to serve for the development of football and not for anything else'.

"On both these promises, he has failed to deliver. The shabby, back room, opaque deal he hatched and tried to force through was anything but transparent."

Later on Saturday, Concacaf joined Uefa in criticising Fifa leadership and said "accountability cannot be optional".

[Lähde: The New York Times | URL: https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7484707/2026/08/01/uefa-gianni-infantino-fifa/]
UEFA says it and “other members of the football family” have lost confidence in Gianni Infantino, accusing the FIFA President of a “shabby, back room, opaque” deal after plans to sell a stake in its competitions were abandoned.

FIFA and Infantino performed a U-turn on the proposals to sell stakes in the World Cup and world football’s governing body’s other tournaments to private investors on Friday following significant backlash, including from European federation UEFA, who vowed to boycott the World Cup in protest.

---

[Lähde: Yahoo Sports | URL: https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/fifa-abandon-20b-world-cup-060500041.html]
FIFA have abandoned plans to sell a minority stake in its commercial business after serious opposition from the global football community and the withdrawal of key investors (New York Post).

It is a major blow to FIFA president Gianni Infantino's leadership.

The governing body had been exploring the sale of a one-fifth stake in a newly created commercial entity.

The deal would have valued the business at around $20 billion and raised approximately $4.2bn.

The proposal involved spinning off FIFA's lucrative television rights, sponsorship agreements, licensing and ticketing operations into a separate company.

However, the project has now been abandoned after Thrive Capital, the investment firm led by Joshua Kushner, reportedly pulled back from the negotiations.

JP Morgan had been advising on the transaction. They have also closed their involvement as support for the proposal evaporated.

Infantino later confirmed the decision, admitting the plan had created divisions within world football that outweighed any potential benefits.

FIFA will continue managing and selling its commercial rights through its existing structure.

The collapse follows fierce resistance from several of football's most influential confederations.

UEFA reportedly warned that its member nations would boycott FIFA competitions if private investors were allowed to take ownership of the sport's commercial assets

Opposition quickly spread beyond Europe, with CONCACAF and the Asian Football Confederation also rejecting the proposal.

Without the backing of the world's biggest football markets, the project became impossible to salvage.

The failed initiative has also exposed deep cracks within FIFA itself.

Chief operating officer Kevin Lamour publicly criticised the process, claiming senior executives had been kept in the dark and describing the proposal as the project of one person rather than FIFA's.

Senior adviser Carlos Cordeiro also resigned over the controversy.

With FIFA's commercial gamble abandoned and pressure growing ahead of next year's presidential election, Infantino's authority appears weaker than ever.

What was intended to modernise FIFA's finances has instead become one of the biggest political setbacks of his presidency, leaving serious questions over whether he should remain in charge.

CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani is set to challenge Infantino, but UEFA-touted Paris Saint-Germain president Nasser al-Khelaifi has no intention to follow suit.

Aug 1 (Reuters) - FIFA President Gianni Infantino is under unprecedented fire after regional confederations UEFA and CONCACAF said on Saturday they had lost confidence in his leadership following his abandoned plan to sell a stake in World Cup commercial rights.

The dramatic fallout from Infantino's scrapped $4.2-billion proposal has exposed growing unease within world soccer over his leadership style, with UEFA leading a chorus of criticism that could complicate his re-election hopes....

payload.title: Paine Infantinoa kohtaan kasvaa – Concacaf vaatii Fifa-johdon perusteellista arviointia
payload.summary: Uefa ja Concacaf arvostelevat Fifan johtamista järjestön luovuttua kaupalliseen toimintaansa liittyneestä sijoittajahankkeesta. Kiista lisää Gianni Infantinoon kohdistuvaa painetta ennen hänen tavoittelemaansa neljättä puheenjohtajakautta.
payload.content:
Jalkapallon kansainvälisen kattojärjestön Fifan puheenjohtajaan Gianni Infantinoon kohdistuva paine kasvaa, kun Euroopan jalkapalloliitto Uefa sekä Pohjois- ja Keski-Amerikan ja Karibian alueen lajiliitto Concacaf ovat arvostelleet julkisesti Fifan johtamista. Lausuntojen taustalla on järjestön päätös luopua suunnitelmasta, jossa yksityisille sijoittajille olisi myyty vähemmistöosuus Fifan kaupallisesta liiketoiminnasta. Suunnitelman peruuntuminen avasi samalla laajemman kiistan järjestön johtamistavasta.

## Uefa nosti esiin Infantinon lupaukset

Uefa ja Concacaf julkaisivat lausuntonsa lauantaina sen jälkeen, kun Infantino ilmoitti, ettei Fifa enää vie sijoittajahanketta eteenpäin. Uefa toivotti vetäytymisen tervetulleeksi ja kuvasi sitä ”voitoksi koko jalkapallolle”. Samalla Euroopan lajiliitto syytti Infantinoa lupaustensa täyttämättä jättämisestä ja viittasi puheeseen, jonka hän piti kampanjoidessaan puheenjohtajaksi vuonna 2016.

Concacaf puolestaan ilmoitti ”yhtenäisyyden voittaneen”. Sen mukaan sijoittajaehdotus oli oire johtamisesta, joka oli lakannut asettamasta jalkapalloa etusijalle. Liitto luonnehti tapausta yksipuoliseksi ja vakavaksi hallinnon sekä johtamisen epäonnistumiseksi ja katsoi sen jatkavan aiempien virheiden ja samanlaisen toiminnan kaavaa. Concacaf vaati Fifan johtamisen perusteellista arviointia, mutta ei maininnut Infantinoa lausunnossaan nimeltä.

Uefa oli ensimmäinen suuri jalkapallon hallintoelin, joka reagoi suunnitelman pois vetämiseen, ja Concacaf seurasi omalla kannanotollaan. Kumpikin piti hankkeen kaatumista myönteisenä, mutta niiden painotukset erosivat: Uefa nimesi Infantinon ja hänen lupauksensa, kun taas Concacaf kohdisti vaatimuksensa Fifan johtoon nimeämättä puheenjohtajaa. Suunnitelman peruuttaminen ei siten päättänyt hallintoa koskevaa arvostelua.

## Kaupallisesta yhtiöstä olisi myyty viidennes

Fifa oli selvittänyt noin viidenneksen suuruisen vähemmistöosuuden myymistä vasta perustettavasta kaupallisesta yhtiöstä. Suunnitelmassa erilliseen yhtiöön olisi koottu järjestön televisio-oikeudet, sponsorisopimukset, lisensointi ja lipunmyynti. Kaupallisen kokonaisuuden arvoksi arvioitiin noin 20 miljardia dollaria, ja osuuden myynnillä olisi kerätty arviolta 4,2 miljardia dollaria. Kyse oli siten useita Fifan keskeisiä kaupallisia toimintoja kattaneesta järjestelystä.

Hankkeesta luovuttiin jalkapalloyhteisössä nousseen voimakkaan vastustuksen ja keskeisten sijoittajien vetäytymisen jälkeen. Joshua Kushnerin johtaman sijoitusyhtiö Thrive Capitalin kerrottiin vetäytyneen neuvotteluista. Järjestelyssä neuvonantajana toiminut JP Morgan lopetti myös osallistumisensa, kun ehdotuksen saama tuki hiipui. Infantino on johtanut Fifaa helmikuusta 2016 lähtien ja tavoittelee neljättä puheenjohtajakautta maaliskuussa järjestettävässä Fifa-kongressissa. Uefan ja Concacafin julkiset kannanotot lisäävät häneen kohdistuvaa painetta ennen kongressia.

FIFA have abandoned plans to sell a minority stake in its commercial business after serious opposition from the global football community and the withdrawal of key investors (New York Post).

It is a major blow to FIFA president Gianni Infantino's leadership.

The governing body had been exploring the sale of a one-fifth stake in a newly created commercial entity.

The deal would have valued the business at around $20 billion and raised approximately $4.2bn.

The proposal involved spinning off FIFA's lucrative television rights, sponsorship agreements, licensing and ticketing operations into a separate company.

However, the project has now been abandoned after Thrive Capital, the investment firm led by Joshua Kushner, reportedly pulled back from the negotiations.

JP Morgan had been advising on the transaction. They have also closed their involvement as support for the proposal evaporated.

Infantino later confirmed the decision, admitting the plan had created divisions within world football that outweighed any potential benefits.

FIFA will continue managing and selling its commercial rights through its existing structure.

The collapse follows fierce resistance from several of football's most influential confederations.

UEFA reportedly warned that its member nations would boycott FIFA competitions if private investors were allowed to take ownership of the sport's commercial assets

Opposition quickly spread beyond Europe, with CONCACAF and the Asian Football Confederation also rejecting the proposal.

Without the backing of the world's biggest football markets, the project became impossible to salvage.

The failed initiative has also exposed deep cracks within FIFA itself.

Chief operating officer Kevin Lamour publicly criticised the process, claiming senior executives had been kept in the dark and describing the proposal as the project of one person rather than FIFA's.

Senior adviser Carlos Cordeiro also resigned over the controversy.

With FIFA's commercial gamble abandoned and pressure growing ahead of next year's presidential election, Infantino's authority appears weaker than ever.

What was intended to modernise FIFA's finances has instead become one of the biggest political setbacks of his presidency, leaving serious questions over whether he should remain in charge.

CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani is set to challenge Infantino, but UEFA-touted Paris Saint-Germain president Nasser al-Khelaifi has no intention to follow suit.

article.content:
Jalkapallon kansainvälisen kattojärjestön Fifan puheenjohtajaan Gianni Infantinoon kohdistuva paine kasvaa, kun Euroopan jalkapalloliitto Uefa sekä Pohjois- ja Keski-Amerikan ja Karibian alueen lajiliitto Concacaf ovat arvostelleet julkisesti Fifan johtamista. Lausuntojen taustalla on järjestön päätös luopua suunnitelmasta, jossa yksityisille sijoittajille olisi myyty vähemmistöosuus Fifan kaupallisesta liiketoiminnasta. Suunnitelman peruuntuminen avasi samalla laajemman kiistan järjestön johtamistavasta.

## Uefa nosti esiin Infantinon lupaukset

Uefa ja Concacaf julkaisivat lausuntonsa lauantaina sen jälkeen, kun Infantino ilmoitti, ettei Fifa enää vie sijoittajahanketta eteenpäin. Uefa toivotti vetäytymisen tervetulleeksi ja kuvasi sitä ”voitoksi koko jalkapallolle”. Samalla Euroopan lajiliitto syytti Infantinoa lupaustensa täyttämättä jättämisestä ja viittasi puheeseen, jonka hän piti kampanjoidessaan puheenjohtajaksi vuonna 2016.

Concacaf puolestaan ilmoitti ”yhtenäisyyden voittaneen”. Sen mukaan sijoittajaehdotus oli oire johtamisesta, joka oli lakannut asettamasta jalkapalloa etusijalle. Liitto luonnehti tapausta yksipuoliseksi ja vakavaksi hallinnon sekä johtamisen epäonnistumiseksi ja katsoi sen jatkavan aiempien virheiden ja samanlaisen toiminnan kaavaa. Concacaf vaati Fifan johtamisen perusteellista arviointia, mutta ei maininnut Infantinoa lausunnossaan nimeltä.

Uefa oli ensimmäinen suuri jalkapallon hallintoelin, joka reagoi suunnitelman pois vetämiseen, ja Concacaf seurasi omalla kannanotollaan. Kumpikin piti hankkeen kaatumista myönteisenä, mutta niiden painotukset erosivat: Uefa nimesi Infantinon ja hänen lupauksensa, kun taas Concacaf kohdisti vaatimuksensa Fifan johtoon nimeämättä puheenjohtajaa. Suunnitelman peruuttaminen ei siten päättänyt hallintoa koskevaa arvostelua.

## Kaupallisesta yhtiöstä olisi myyty viidennes

Fifa oli selvittänyt noin viidenneksen suuruisen vähemmistöosuuden myymistä vasta perustettavasta kaupallisesta yhtiöstä. Suunnitelmassa erilliseen yhtiöön olisi koottu järjestön televisio-oikeudet, sponsorisopimukset, lisensointi ja lipunmyynti. Kaupallisen kokonaisuuden arvoksi arvioitiin noin 20 miljardia dollaria, ja osuuden myynnillä olisi kerätty arviolta 4,2 miljardia dollaria. Kyse oli siten useita Fifan keskeisiä kaupallisia toimintoja kattaneesta järjestelystä.

Hankkeesta luovuttiin jalkapalloyhteisössä nousseen voimakkaan vastustuksen ja keskeisten sijoittajien vetäytymisen jälkeen. Joshua Kushnerin johtaman sijoitusyhtiö Thrive Capitalin kerrottiin vetäytyneen neuvotteluista. Järjestelyssä neuvonantajana toiminut JP Morgan lopetti myös osallistumisensa, kun ehdotuksen saama tuki hiipui. Infantino on johtanut Fifaa helmikuusta 2016 lähtien ja tavoittelee neljättä puheenjohtajakautta maaliskuussa järjestettävässä Fifa-kongressissa. Uefan ja Concacafin julkiset kannanotot lisäävät häneen kohdistuvaa painetta ennen kongressia.
